catalog_quote: Aunque no hay indicación de que Steffel reconoció la importancia contrastiva del acento, el registro que legó hace evidente que la acentuación era imprevisible y fonémica, como se demuestra en los siguientes dos pares mínimos: guacá, ‘para acá’ ≠ guáca, ‘flecha’ y hulí, ‘otro’ ≠ húli, ‘sí’. [...] Casi todas las palabras (97%) muestran un sólo acento en una de las tres primeras sílabas y en casi dos tercios (60%), el acento recae sobre la segunda sílaba. El acento en la segunda sílaba es el patrón dominante en las palabras de dos o cuatro sílabas, mientras que el acento en palabras de tres sílabas, cae casi equitativamente en la segunda y la tercera sílabas.

The passage is explicitly Villalpando's summary of the unpub…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In the CET (1992) dialect survey the 'Norte' variety patterns with Centro/Cumbre/Sur against Oeste on a stress isogloss: in the diagnostic words (makói 'ten', sinówi 'snake', sikúi 'ant') Norte has penultimate stress where Western Tarahumara has final stress. This is a lexically restricted isogloss note, not a general word-stress rule; general descriptions of neighbouring Alta-Tarahumara varieties (Brambila 1953:245 Norogachi, itself a CET-'Norte' locality; Caballero 2022 Choguita) describe lexically contrastive stress confined to an initial three-syllable window.
new_statements.exceptions: None; only three lexical items are given, and the Norte cell is filled for all three.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms from a dialect-survey wordlist; statement is comparative (Oeste vs the rest), reported second-hand by Villalpando from the unpublished CET 1992 report. CET/INALI 'Norte' = Sisoguichi–Narárachi–Carichí–Norogachi area (INALI additionally lists Guerrero municipality: Arisiachi, Tomochi, La Nopalera), i.e. wider than and not identical to Ethnologue/Glottolog thh (Ariseachi group).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog nort2956 carries ISO thh = Ethnologue 'Northern Tarahumara / Ariseachi Tarahumara': Santa Rosa Ariseachi, Agua Caliente Ariseachi, Bilaguchi, Tomochi, La Nopalera (Guerrero municipality, Chihuahua; Glottolog coordinates 28.46,-107.80 sit by Tomochi); 300 elderly speakers in 1993, 'may be extinct'. The only stress statement found concerns the CET 1992 / INALI 2008 'tarahumara del norte' (ralámuli raicha Norte), a much wider unit sampled at Sisoguichi, Narárachi, Carichí, Ocórare, Pasigochi and Norogachi (Bocoyna/Carichí area; INALI also lists the Guerrero-municipality thh localities under it). Most of that area is Central Tarahumara [tar] in Ethnologue/Glottolog terms (Caballero 2022: Ethnologue Central = INALI Central + Norte; Norogachi is ISO tar). No first-hand linguistic description of the Ariseachi/Tomochi communities themselves was located.

new_statements.quote: Aunque no hay indicación de que Steffel reconoció la importancia contrastiva del acento, el registro que legó hace evidente que la acentuación era imprevisible y fonémica, como se demuestra en los siguientes dos pares mínimos: guacá, ‘para acá’ ≠ guáca, ‘flecha’ y hulí, ‘otro’ ≠ húli, ‘sí’. [...] Casi todas las palabras (97%) muestran un sólo acento en una de las tres primeras sílabas y en casi dos tercios (60%), el acento recae sobre la segunda sílaba. El acento en la segunda sílaba es el patrón dominante en las palabras de dos o cuatro sílabas, mientras que el acento en palabras de tres sílabas, cae casi equitativamente en la segunda y la tercera sílabas.
new_statements.translation: Although there is no indication that Steffel recognised the contrastive importance of the accent, the record he left makes it evident that accentuation was unpredictable and phonemic, as shown by the following two minimal pairs: guacá 'towards here' ≠ guáca 'arrow' and hulí 'other' ≠ húli 'yes'. [...] Almost all words (97%) show a single accent on one of the first three syllables, and in almost two thirds (60%) the accent falls on the second syllable. Second-syllable accent is the dominant pattern in words of two or four syllables, whereas in three-syllable words the accent falls almost equally on the second and the third syllables.

new_statements.relation_note: Stress phonemic/unpredictable within first three syllables; no mention of tone.
new_statements.rule_in_words: In the 18th-century Tarahumara recorded by Steffel (mostly Tomochic district, 1763-65), word stress is lexically contrastive and not predictable (minimal pairs guacá/guáca, hulí/húli), but confined to an initial three-syllable window: 97% of 1086 reliably accented words carry one stress on the 1st, 2nd or 3rd syllable (9% / 60% / 28%); disyllables are 94% final(=2nd)-stressed, trisyllables split 42% second vs 47% third, 4-syllable words 72% second. This matches the initial three-syllable stress window described for modern Rarámuri varieties (Choguita, Norogachi).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Merrill: about 2% of words are written with two accents (compounds, words with inherently stressed suffixes -simí, -rúgame/-túgame, -guí, some 6-syllable words on 2nd+4th); 'es imposible determinar si el doble acento representaba dos acentos de la misma intensidad o el acento primario y secundario' (p.731). Steffel's acute vs grave accent difference is typographical, not primary/secondary (ch.7.3 p.453).
new_statements.exceptions: Single stress on the 4th syllable in 7-8 words (interrogative -tsá final stress; talahumáli possibly Spanish-influenced); locative -tschíc stressed in 2-4-syllable words but unstressed in 5-syllable words with exceptions; stressed suffixes -simí, -rúgame ~ -túgame, -guí keep their stress regardless of word length; participial -ameke unstressed; one 7-syllable word stressed on the 5th; a few enigmatic double-accented forms (pp.727-731).
new_statements.identity_note: Historical stage (1761-1767) of the speech of the Tomochic mission district. Ch.1 p.78: in 1763 Steffel took over 'Tomochic y sus tres visitas Ariséachic, Cajurichic y Paguéachic' (until early 1766); p.106: 'La mayor parte de la información que incorporó a su diccionario proviene probablemente de la región de Tomochic, donde pasó casi la mitad de todo el tiempo que estuvo en las misiones de la Tarahumara'. Tomochi and (Santa Rosa) Ariseachi are two of the five towns Ethnologue lists for Northern Tarahumara [thh] (Guerrero municipality, Chihuahua; Glottolog coordinates sit by Tomochi). Caveats: Steffel also served at Tónachic (1.5 y), Nonoava (6 m) and San Borja (9 m), so some material may be Central/eastern; and 250 years separate this corpus from the moribund modern variety. No separate glottocode exists for Steffel's doculect (Glottolog files Steffel 1809 under Tarahumara generally, not under nort2956).

Cuadro 5 (p.27): CET 'Norte' area = Sisoguichi, Narárachi, Carichí, Ocórare, Pasigochi, Norogachi. Second-hand, lexically restricted isogloss statement; the thesis itself describes Turuachi (Southeastern, tcu).
